title: Nightshift vector-dim glitch notes
notes:
Timestamp: 2026-05-10 02:45-03:30 UTC (nightshift window)

High-level summary:
- Small production incident observed during late-night traffic: reranking endpoint started returning 500s for a handful of customers while the embeddings endpoint returned 200s.
- Root visible symptom: downstream service complains about embedding vector dimensionality (mismatch between expected and actual).
- Also saw a correlated p95 latency spike for embedding calls around 03:14 UTC (from baseline ~120ms -> 1.2s).

What I observed (raw):
- Customer trace id: trace-0x9fa2c (attached in logs)
- Example error from rerank service: "ValueError: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1024 got 1536 (input id abc123)"
- Embeddings service logs around same trace: "INFO: model=redwood-embed-xq:1.2 output_dim=1536 request_id=trace-0x9fa2c latency_ms=1180"
- Upstream embed HTTP response still 200 with payload: {"id":"abc123","embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ...] } — no explicit error there.

Commands / queries I ran (local repro and prod probes):
1) curl probe to embeddings (to confirm dims):
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RWD_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-xq:1.2", "input": "test"}' https://api.redwood/v1/embeddings | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
   => 1536

2) curl to rerank service with same shape header: (expected 1024)
   curl -s -X POST https://internal/rerank -d '{"embedding": [..1536..] }'
   => HTTP 500 with stack: ValueError dimension mismatch

3) Snapshot of routing table /model aliases used in prod:
   rgrep -n "embed-" deployments/* | sed -n '1,200p'
   Observed: alias "embed-default" points to redwood-embed-xq:1.2 as of 2026-05-09 22:07 UTC (recent rollout)

4) Quick GPU memory / kernel probe on staging model replicas (via srun):
   python infra/inspect_model.py --model redwood-embed-xq:1.2 --metrics
   => qkv-kernel=opt-v2, runtime-path=quantized-int4, output-dim=1536

5) Small-batch vs large-batch reproductions:
   - single-input -> embed dim 1536, latency 110ms on dedicated node (non-prod)
   - batch of 16 -> embed dim 1536, latency increases to ~720ms (batching overhead + kernel).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model rollout created a new embedding model with different output dim (1536) and the rerank service still expects 1024. Alias mapping changed. Rollout window around 2026-05-09 22:07 UTC matches incident start. (LIKELY)
2) Quantized variant selection path incorrectly returns a compatibility alias (redwood-embed-xq) that was not added to rerank's compatibility matrix. Rerank's infer-time validation should catch this but maybe disabled for perf. (LIKELY)
3) Client-side post-processing truncation/serialization bug — unlikely because embed service returns proper length and we saw the raw embedding length in logs. (LESS LIKELY)
4) A stale service mesh sidecar cached an older model signature and performed a transformation incorrectly. (POSSIBLE but no evidence)

What I tried (mitigations / quick fixes):
- Temporarily pinned embed alias for impacted customers to embed-1024-v2 via routing override for their account (quick rollback) — mitigated errors for affected customers within ~6 minutes.
- Added a short-term validation in rerank to early-return a 400 with a helpful message when dim != expected instead of 500. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-service/pull/987 (WIP).
- Opened JIRA ticket JIRA-EMBED-789 to track model onboarding checklist failures (missing dim metadata).

Data collected / evidence saved:
- Kibana logs: embeddings.logs: index 2026-05-10, tag embed-xq:1.2 (downloaded)
- Flame graph + p95 snapshots for embedding node around incident (saved to /tmp/nightshift-flames.tgz)
- Example payloads (sanitized) saved: /tmp/nightshift-example-payloads.json

Immediate next steps (for morning team):
- Confirm whether embed alias redwood-embed-xq:1.2 was intentionally bumped to 1536 by model-onboarding (Priya). If so, we need a cross-service rollout plan: update rerank compatibility matrix AND create a transitional adapter.
- Add automatic model-metadata propagation: embedding_service should publish output_dim to service-discovery / model-registry so downstreams auto-validate.
- Add alert: embed-dim-change (metric: model.output_dim != historical_dim) to catch future rollouts that alter vector size.
- Investigate latency cause for quantized variant: p95 jumped to 1.2s — is kernel selection falling back to slower path for some sequences? Attach kernel debug logs.
- Schedule postmortem if more than 3 customers impacted. (So far only 2 noticed; we patched quickly).

Longer-term notes / ideas:
- Rerank service should accept a small set of dims (1024, 1536) if algorithm tolerates, but prefer explicit version compatibility.
- Consider adding a schema endpoint on embeddings API: GET /v1/models/{id}/metadata -> { output_dim: 1536, quantized: true, kernel: opt-v2 } and have orchestration push to downstreams.
- When onboarding new embed models, require a smoke test that runs against rerank, search, and other consumers (a short matrix test).

Questions for morning sync:
- Who owns the redwood-embed-xq alias rollout? (Priya?)
- Do we have any customers still receiving 1536 that we didn't mitigate? (CS to confirm)
- Should we force a read-only flag to prevent further alias changes until model-registry metadata propagation is implemented?

Notes-to-self: keep this doc as a running breadcrumb list while followups happen. If I don't come back to it, morning handoff: Priya, Evelyn, Tomás.

Relevant snippets (copied from logs):
[embed-service] 2026-05-10T03:14:21Z INFO model=redwood-embed-xq:1.2 output_dim=1536 request_id=trace-0x9fa2c latency_ms=1180
[rerank-service] 2026-05-10T03:14:21Z ERROR ValueError embedding dim mismatch expected=1024 got=1536 trace=trace-0x9fa2c

Quick repro script (local):
python - <<'PY'
import requests, os
h={'Authorization':f'Bearer {os.environ.get("RWD_KEY")}', 'Content-Type':'application/json'}
r = requests.post('https://api.redwood/v1/embeddings', json={'model':'redwood-embed-xq:1.2','input':'debug test'}, headers=h)
print('dim', len(r.json()['data'][0]['embedding']))
PY

If anyone is debugging this later, start by confirming model-registry metadata (model_registry.get('redwood-embed-xq:1.2')) and then check the alias history in infra/alias-audit.
